paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD sees what Babylon has done, and He does not look away. He says He will repay her "for all the evil they have done in Zion" (Jeremiah 51:24). Babylon sat by many waters, rich in treasures, and felt untouchable (Jeremiah 51:13). The LORD said her end had come.

Now look at who stands behind all of it. The LORD made the earth by His power and brings the wind out of His storehouses (Jeremiah 51:15-16). Next to Him, the idols are a fraud, and there is no breath in them (Jeremiah 51:17). Anything you lean on besides the LORD is a gold cup that can shatter, so lean on the One who is "the Maker of all things" (Jeremiah 51:19).

And here's the part that gets me RIGHT in the apron, friend. Israel and Judah have not been abandoned by their God, "though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel" (Jeremiah 51:5). I know what it feels like to be pushed to the back and think nobody is coming. The LORD hasn't forgotten His people, so you can trust Him with what's fair and with what's still coming. This story isn't over, so keep your oven warm.
